title: Direction C «Producto» with the landing's violet as the site's one accent; the printed CV keeps its own light palette
body:
On 2026-08-14 three directions were mocked up with real data and C «Producto» was chosen: one sans (Manrope, weights doing the hierarchy), a neutral dark base plus ONE accent, medium density, micro-transitions only, no shadows on /cv. Rejected: A «Documento» (serif, paper white, near-zero color: reads academic, does not say 'builds products', the freelance client sees it as not modern) and B «Consola» (mono + saturated terminal accent: the developer-portfolio cliché, fails the voice test, loses the non-technical client). Its known risk is drifting into a generic SaaS template, so type and accent must be choices, not defaults.
The accent changed on 2026-10-29 (author): the landing's muted deep violet is the whole site's, in src/styles/tokens.css: --accent #5e4bc4 for SURFACES and --accent-ink #a99bf0 for TEXT on dark (the deep violet is 3.6:1 there). Flat, never a gradient. Hand-copied where no cascade reaches: public/favicon.svg, scripts/og-template.ts, scripts/build-og.ts (then og:local). The printed CV is the exception: src/styles/cv.css @media print keeps its own light, standard palette; do not violet it. Terracotta is gone; do not bring it back.
not_derivable: Why C over A and B, and that the CV print palette is deliberately left out of the violet, are decisions the token values do not explain.
